**Bottom line:** The clause is a valid liquidated-damages provision, not a penalty — a customary 5% earnest-money deposit was a reasonable forecast of the Sellers' speculative loss at the time of contracting. The Buyers' conceded failure to close triggered it; the Sellers' marketing (authorized by the Buyers' own attorney) and backup offer expressly contingent on the Buyers' nonperformance was mitigation, not waiver; and the higher $360,000 resale doesn't defeat the stipulated remedy. The Sellers keep the $17,750 deposit; the Buyers get no refund.
